target_audience: First-year university calculus students or advanced high school students

sections.title: The 'Hidden' Variable: Explicit vs. Implicit
lecture_lines: Explicit functions like y equals f of x are clear.
Implicit relations like circles tangle x and y together.
We still need the slope, dy dx, everywhere.
animations: Display 'y = x^2' (Blue #00AAFF) and 'x^2 + y^2 = 25' (Orange #FFA500).
Draw a simple blue line and orange circle side-by-side.
Highlight 'y' in the circle equation with a pulsing red (#FF0000).
Add a white tangent line (#FFFFFF) on the orange circle at (3, 4).
A small white triangle (drone) moves along the circle path.

sections.title: Prerequisite Tool: The Chain Rule Review
lecture_lines: The chain rule handles functions nested inside others.
Differentiating y cubed gives three y squared times dy dx.
Always multiply by the derivative of the inner function.
animations: Show 'd/dx[f(x)]^3 = 3[f(x)]^2 * f'(x)' in yellow (#FFFF00).
Show 'd/dx[y^3]' transforming into '3y^2 * (dy/dx)' with dy/dx in red (#FF0000).
Three gears labeled 'x' (blue), 'y' (green), 'dy/dx' (red) rotating together.

sections.title: The Four-Step Process
lecture_lines: First, differentiate both sides of the equation.
Apply the chain rule to every term containing y.
Group all terms with dy dx on one side.
Factor out dy dx and isolate it.
The result is our formula for the slope.
animations: Display 'x^2 + y^2 = 25' with x terms blue (#00AAFF), y terms green (#00FF00).
Prefix both sides with 'd/dx' symbols in white (#FFFFFF).
Change 'x^2' to '2x' and 'y^2' to '2y * dy/dx' (dy/dx in red #FF0000).
Move '2x' to the right side, making it '-2x' via sliding animation.
Isolate 'dy/dx' by moving '2y' to the denominator on the right.

sections.title: Graphical Interpretation & Verification
lecture_lines: Let's verify our formula on the circle's graph.
At point three four, the slope is negative three fourths.
The formula matches the visual tangent line perfectly.
animations: Draw orange circle (#FFA500) with a white tangent line at (3, 4).
Text 'dy/dx = -3/4' appears next to the tangent point in white.
Snail icon (White #FFFFFF) slides down the tangent line grade.

sections.title: Complex Application: The Folium of Descartes
lecture_lines: Complex loops like this are hard to solve for y.
Implicit differentiation makes finding the slope much easier.
Use the product rule on terms like six x y.
Six x y becomes six y plus six x dy dx.
Combine these rules to master any complex curve.
animations: Draw Folium curve (Purple #BF00FF) and equation 'x^3 + y^3 = 6xy'.
Transform left side to '3x^2 + 3y^2 * dy/dx' in white.
Transform right side to '6y + 6x * dy/dx' using the product rule.
Move all terms with 'dy/dx' to the left side of the equation.
Factor out 'dy/dx' and display the final fractional result.

sections.title: Summary & Key Takeaways
lecture_lines: Remember: always tag y derivatives with dy dx.
Isolate dy dx to find the rate of change.
You can now differentiate any relation, no matter how messy.
animations: Display 'Whenever differentiating y, multiply by dy/dx' in Gold (#FFD700).
Checklist appears: 'Chain Rule?', 'Isolate dy/dx?', 'Slope found?' with green checks (#00FF00).
The 'dy/dx' symbol pulses in bright green (#00FF00) for emphasis.
